Suspected Responsible Party: USCG STA PORT ANGELES
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 47.948924, -123.347650 (Approximated from ZIP)
Reported Spill Volume: 0 gallons
Report Description
WHILE FUELING THE 45602, A USCG ASSET, THE FUELING TEAM INCORRECTLY SOUNDED THE FUEL TANK. THE FUELING TEAM PUMPED TOO MUCH DIESEL FUEL INTO THE TANK. THE TANK BURPED DIESEL FUEL THROUGH THE VENT. THE VENT IS CONTAINED, BUT SOME FUEL RAN DOWN THE BULKHEAD. THE FUELING TEAM IMMEDIATELY RESPONDED WITH ABSORBANT PADS AND DEPLOYED A PORTABLE BOOM. THE TEAM WAS UNABLE TO SEE A SHEEN, AS THE INCIDENT OCCURRED AT NIGHT, BUT THEY BELIEVE AN AMOUNT OF LESS THAN AN OUNCE ENTERED THE WATER. THEY USED ABSORBANT PADS TO SKIM THE WATER, BUT COULD NOT DETECT ANY SHEEN OR DIESEL FUEL SMELL ON THE PADS.

Report Details

Nearest City: Montville Twp, OH
Location: 4595 SHARON COPLEY ROAD (STATE ROUTE 162) 4595 SHARON COPLEY ROAD (STATE ROUTE 162
Incident Type: PIPELINE
Material: NATURAL GAS
Medium Affected: LAND
Suspected Responsible Party: ATLAS ENERGY
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 41.106643, -81.837731 (Approximated from route)
Report Description
[WEB REPORT] MONTVILLE TWP. — STATE ROUTE 162 WAS CLOSED FOR SEVERAL HOURS WEDNESDAY FOR CLEANUP OF A NATURAL GAS LEAK IN FRONT OF A HOME. A MONTVILLE POLICE SGT. SAID A RESIDENT AT 4595 SHARON COPLEY ROAD (STATE ROUTE 162) WAS RIDING HIS LAWN MOWER AT ABOUT 11:30 A.M. WHEN HE STRUCK A GAS WELL CONNECTION IN HIS FRONT YARD CLOSE TO THE ROADWAY. “IT LOOKED VERY SIMILAR TO A GEYSER,” LAFOND SAID. “IT WAS SPILLING A YELLOWISH CLOUD INTO THE AIR.” LAFOND SAID NO ONE WAS INJURED AND NO ONE HAD TO BE EVACUATED. THE MEDINA FIRE CHIEF SAID THE GAS CLOUD ROSE ABOUT 15 TO 20 FEET ABOVE THE POWER LINES. THE FIRE CHIEF SAID THE PIPELINE IS FIVE MILES OF 5-INCH PIPE. IT TRANSMITS NATURAL GAS FROM LOCAL WELLS, HE SAID. OIL ALSO SPILLED ONTO THE ROAD, AND THE FIRE DEPARTMENT AND POLICE PUT DOWN SAND TO SOAK IT UP. HE SAID HE WASN’T SURE HOW MUCH OIL AND GAS LEAKED. HE SAID REPRESENTATIVES FROM THE COMPANY TOOK ABOUT A HALF-HOUR TO GET TO THE SCENE, BUT THEY WERE ABLE TO SHUT OFF VALVES AND CLEAN UP THE LEAK. THE ROAD WAS CLOSED BETWEEN STATE ROUTES 57 AND 3, EXCEPT TO LOCAL TRAFFIC, UNTIL ABOUT 6 P.M. WEDNESDAY.

Lat/Long: 41.106643, -81.837731 (Approximated from route)
Report Description
[WEB REPORT] MONTVILLE TWP. — STATE ROUTE 162 WAS CLOSED FOR SEVERAL HOURS WEDNESDAY FOR CLEANUP OF A NATURAL GAS LEAK IN FRONT OF A HOME. A MONTVILLE POLICE SGT. SAID A RESIDENT AT 4595 SHARON COPLEY ROAD (STATE ROUTE 162) WAS RIDING HIS LAWN MOWER AT ABOUT 11:30 A.M. WHEN HE STRUCK A GAS WELL CONNECTION IN HIS FRONT YARD CLOSE TO THE ROADWAY. “IT LOOKED VERY SIMILAR TO A GEYSER,” LAFOND SAID. “IT WAS SPILLING A YELLOWISH CLOUD INTO THE AIR.” LAFOND SAID NO ONE WAS INJURED AND NO ONE HAD TO BE EVACUATED. THE MEDINA FIRE CHIEF SAID THE GAS CLOUD ROSE ABOUT 15 TO 20 FEET ABOVE THE POWER LINES. THE FIRE CHIEF SAID THE PIPELINE IS FIVE MILES OF 5-INCH PIPE. IT TRANSMITS NATURAL GAS FROM LOCAL WELLS, HE SAID. OIL ALSO SPILLED ONTO THE ROAD, AND THE FIRE DEPARTMENT AND POLICE PUT DOWN SAND TO SOAK IT UP. HE SAID HE WASN’T SURE HOW MUCH OIL AND GAS LEAKED. HE SAID REPRESENTATIVES FROM THE COMPANY TOOK ABOUT A HALF-HOUR TO GET TO THE SCENE, BUT THEY WERE ABLE TO SHUT OFF VALVES AND CLEAN UP THE LEAK. THE ROAD WAS CLOSED BETWEEN STATE ROUTES 57 AND 3, EXCEPT TO LOCAL TRAFFIC, UNTIL ABOUT 6 P.M. WEDNESDAY.

properties.content:
Report Details
NRC Report ID: 1072070
Incident Time: 2014-01-25 03:00:00
Nearest City: Pascagoula, MS
Location: WEST QUAYWALL SINGING RIVER ISLAND 100 SINGING RIVER ISLAND
Incident Type: VESSEL
Material: OIL, FUEL: NO. 2
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: USCGC DECISIVE
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 30.403992, -88.764950 (Approximated from ZIP)
Reported Sheen Size: 1 feet by 10 feet (area 10 sq. ft.)
Reported Spill Volume: 4 gallon
SkyTruth Minimum Estimate: 0 gallons
Report Description
****WEB REPORT**** APPROXIMATELY 0300 LOCAL, WATCHSTANDER FOUND MGO FUEL OIL TRICKLING FROM THE SOUNDING TUBE AND VENT FOR THE PORT PROPULSION FUEL SERVICE TANK. THE SOUNDING TUBE IS INTERNAL TO THE SHIP, BUT THE VENT IS LOCATED ON THE WEATHER DECK AND ALLOWED FUEL TO ENTER THE WATERSTREAM. SUSPECTED NATURE OF THE OVERFLOW WAS DUE TO THE ONLINE BOILER FUEL RETURN TO THIS TANK WHILE FUEL SUCTION WAS FROM THE STARBOARD FUEL SERVICE TANK. WATCHSTANDER SECURED THE BOILER, CLOSED THE PORT SERVICE TANK FUEL RETURN VALVE, AND PLACED A STOPPER OVER THE WEATHER DECK DRAIN. THE BOILER WAS THE ONLY PIECE OF EQUIPMENT ONLINE. TECHNICAL DATA ESTIMATES 10 GALLONS OF FUEL RETURNED TO THIS TANK FROM THE BOILER FOR THE TIME IT WAS ONLINE. WITH THE PORT SERVICE TANK AT 95%, THE INTRODUCTION OF ADDITIONAL FUEL WITHOUT SUCTION CAUSED A STATIC PRESSURE HEAD TO DEVELOP ULTIMATELY OVER-PRESSURIZING THE TANK AND CAUSING THE OVERFLOW. BASED ON THE AMOUNT OF FUEL THAT OVERFLOWED, IT IS ESTIMATED THAT A GALLON OR LESS ENTERED THE WATERSTREAM. A HARD BOOM WAS ALREADY IN PLACE AROUND THE SHIP AS PER NORMAL MOORING PROCEDURES, BUT A SORBENT BOOM WAS ALSO DEPLOYED TO CAPTURE AS MUCH OF THE HAZARD AS POSSIBLE. ALL SPENT MATERIALS WILL BE CAPTURED AND CONTAINED FOR DISPOSAL. WEATHER CONDITIONS: PRESSURE 1024.5 MB, WIND 0 KTS, SEAS CALM, TEMPERATURE 36-DEG F, PRECIPITATION SNOW/RAIN. THERE IS A VERY SLIGHT CURRENT THAT IS PUSHING ALL OVERFLOWED HAZARD AGAINST THE SHIP AIDING IN RECOVER.
